added_failures_note: Derived with reckon.crew.review.added_failures_from_gate_logs over the reviewed run's own declared suite arms: logs/baseline-suite-base.txt (revision 69fab1372f, scratch tree base-69fab137, '58 passed in 39.73s', EXIT=0) and logs/after-suite-head.txt (revision 4fcb673bca, worktree, '58 passed in 39.65s', EXIT=0) are both pytest-format and neither lists a failing id, so the head adds no failing test and the count is a measured 0 rather than an unread absence. The instrument was shown to see a known failure before the empty arms were reported: the same helper reads the two failing ids out of logs/negative-control-base-target.txt (test_a_queued_reflex_review_carries_the_waiver_and_launches and test_an_implementation_dispatch_in_the_same_state_records_the_backlog) and none out of logs/gate-all_debug-head-final.txt.

findings.text: after_suite records its arm at revision 4fcb673bca, the run's first commit, not at the head 5e2d47e003 the fence asks the after arm to record; the arm's result still stands because the three later commits touch only the evidence fragment, but a reader comparing the pair against the promoted commits cannot tell from the record that the head was measured, and logs/gate-all_debug-head-final.txt repeats the gap by naming 894e759a35 in its header.

the fragment states the head arm carries '98 failing-or-erroring ids' while its own logs/import-arm-head.txt summary reads '89 failed, 1691 passed, 56 warnings, 13 errors' - 102; the 98 comes from logs/head-ids.txt, which strips parametrisation so four distinct parametrised ids collapse into their base id, so the figure disagrees with the log it cites even though the id-set comparison it supports (0 ids only at head, 16 only at base) reproduces under reckon.crew.review.added_failures_from_gate_logs.

terminal_verdict is named 19 lines below the arm at line 1780 that already spells the same predicate as 'manifest_status == "complete" and not deferred_outcome', leaving three spellings of one rule in the function (1780, 1799-1801, 2063); a later edit to the complete arm can drift from the named verdict without reddening anything, which is the disagreement the new comment says the name exists to prevent.

the guard the repair rests on is not deterministic on this host: one run of the named file at head 5e2d47e003 reddened with the base arm's own two ids and the message 'the run is not awaiting review (running)' (logs/reviewed-node-gate-rerun.txt in review run r-20261116T163737912029, '2 failed, 2 passed in 2.52s', EXIT=1), while six further identical runs and the reviewed run's own job 1320281 read '4 passed'; the cause is not established here, and its effect is that a single red at head cannot be told from a regression from the log's wording alone.

item_verdicts.done_when: The done_when asks for the file passing in full as an all_debug job with SLURM_JOB_ID unset, an importing-test arm adding no failure, and a base negative control; logs/gate-all_debug-head-final.txt carries '# slurm_job 1320281' with the env -u SLURM_JOB_ID command, logs/negative-control-base-target.txt reads '2 failed, 2 passed in 2.67s' EXIT=1 at 69fab1372f, and the two importing arms differ by 0 ids at head and 16 at base.

item_verdicts.manifest: manifest.md in the run directory reads status complete, four commits 4fcb673bca/4bf1ae4afe/894e759a35/5e2d47e003, the named file green at 894e759a with EXIT=0, the base arm red 2 failed of 4, the 216-module importing arm, and both suite arms at 58 passed EXIT=0.
